english: Let $C$ be the parabola $y^{2}-2y-5x+6=0$, and let $P(\alpha,\beta)$ be a point from which the two tangents drawn to $C$ are perpendicular to each other and whose chord of contact with respect to $C$ is parallel to the line $2x+y=0$. Then the value of $\alpha+\beta$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $C$ परवलय $y^{2}-2y-5x+6=0$ है, तथा $P(\alpha,\beta)$ एक ऐसा बिन्दु है जिससे $C$ पर खींची गई दोनों स्पर्श रेखाएँ परस्पर लम्बवत् हैं और $C$ के सापेक्ष जिसकी स्पर्श जीवा रेखा $2x+y=0$ के समान्तर है। तब $\alpha+\beta$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Perpendicular tangents meet on the directrix (the director circle of a parabola): $\alpha=-\dfrac{1}{4}$
solution_full: Completing the square: $y^{2}-2y+1=5x-5$, so $C:\ (y-1)^{2}=5(x-1)$. With $X=x-1$, $Y=y-1$ this is $Y^{2}=4AX$, $A=\dfrac{5}{4}$; vertex $(1,1)$, axis $y=1$, directrix $X=-A$, i.e. $x=1-\dfrac{5}{4}=-\dfrac{1}{4}$.
The locus of points from which two perpendicular tangents can be drawn to a parabola (its director circle) is the directrix. Hence $\alpha=-\dfrac{1}{4}$.
The chord of contact of $(X_{1},Y_{1})$ for $Y^{2}=4AX$ is $YY_{1}=2A(X+X_{1})$. Here $X_{1}=\alpha-1$, $Y_{1}=\beta-1$: $(\beta-1)(y-1)=\dfrac{5}{2}(x-1+\alpha-1)$.

Its slope is $\dfrac{5}{2(\beta-1)}$ (note $\beta\neq1$, otherwise the chord would be vertical). Parallel to $2x+y=0$ means slope $-2$: $\dfrac{5}{2(\beta-1)}=-2$, so $\beta-1=-\dfrac{5}{4}$, $\beta=-\dfrac{1}{4}$.

Check: $P\left(-\dfrac{1}{4},-\dfrac{1}{4}\right)$ is outside $C$, since $\left(-\dfrac{5}{4}\right)^{2}-5\left(-\dfrac{5}{4}\right)>0$; the tangents from $P$ have slopes $m$ with $m^{2}-m-1=0$, product $-1$.
originality_note: New: a point fixed by two conditions on a shifted parabola, perpendicular tangents (placing it on the directrix) and the direction of its chord of contact (fixing the other coordinate) (way 3). Closest known: 'locus of the point of intersection of perpendicular tangents is the directrix' and chord-of-contact exercises. Different because: the two conditions together pin down a single point, and the shifted form must be handled in both.

concept_use.Director circle for parabola: The locus of points with perpendicular tangents (the director circle of a parabola) is its directrix x = -1/4, which gives alpha.
concept_use.tangents drawn from an external point to: The chord of contact of P for the two tangents from P, (beta - 1)(y - 1) = (5/2)(x + alpha - 2), is made parallel to 2x + y = 0, which gives beta.
